Title: Week 01: Define FaultAdapt-Gym scope and compute budget
Technical / research work: Audit CPU/RAM and time constraints; install the package; run the smoke experiment; define the exact primary question and exclusions.
Exit criterion: Clean installation, passing smoke run, one-page scope and compute inventory.
Relationship / public action: List relevant UoM controls/robotics/ML mentors and request one bounded proposal critique.

Title: Week 02: Reproduce control and RL foundations
Technical / research work: Review MDPs, PPO, recurrent policies, partial observability, and online system identification; reproduce a Pendulum baseline.
Exit criterion: Seeded Pendulum baseline with environment lock and first learning/control plot.
Relationship / public action: Follow maintainers and two relevant labs; write technical notes rather than generic messages.

Title: Week 03: Build the adaptive-control literature matrix
Technical / research work: Read 6–8 anchor works on adaptive/meta-RL, fault-tolerant control, recurrent RL, and system identification.
Exit criterion: Literature matrix with problem, hidden context, method, metrics, limitations, and open gap.
Relationship / public action: Discuss the gap with one postgraduate student or faculty member.

Title: Week 04: Freeze the two-page proposal and pilot
Technical / research work: Specify H1–H4, methods, independent/dependent variables, compute cap, risks, and run one sudden-fault pilot.
Exit criterion: Mentor-reviewed proposal and go/no-go decision for Reacher and method scope.
Relationship / public action: Send the proposal to a second local academic only if its scope is concrete.

Title: Week 05: Complete fault wrappers and deterministic harness
Technical / research work: Test fixed, sudden, and gradual actuator loss plus delay, noise, and bias; add seeded evaluation configuration.
Exit criterion: Wrapper unit tests and deterministic rollout/evaluation tests pass.
Relationship / public action: Open an upstream issue only for a genuine reproducible Gymnasium/SB3 problem.

Title: Week 06: Implement classical baseline and provenance logging
Technical / research work: Implement the environment-appropriate classical controller and log config, seed, commit, timing, and raw results.
Exit criterion: Classical baseline evaluated across nominal and initial fault sweep.
Relationship / public action: Publish a short note explaining control assumptions and failure conditions.

Title: Week 07: Train feed-forward PPO under fixed budgets
Technical / research work: Add a small feed-forward PPO baseline; tune only using a declared budget.
Exit criterion: One- to two-seed debug results plus five-seed nominal baseline if runtime permits.
Relationship / public action: Ask one RL practitioner for feedback on evaluation fairness, not model tuning.

Title: Week 08: Release benchmark v0.1
Technical / research work: Package installation, plotting, result schema, and first baseline sweep.
Exit criterion: A clean environment reproduces tests and one fault plot; tagged v0.1 release.
Relationship / public action: Post the first technical progress update and request feedback on one precise design choice.

Title: Week 09: Implement recurrent PPO
Technical / research work: Add a GRU/LSTM policy receiving interaction history without ground-truth fault labels.
Exit criterion: Recurrent policy trains and evaluation verifies that hidden fault state is not exposed.
Relationship / public action: Study AMAGO and contact an accessible maintainer/author only with a code-level question.

Title: Week 10: Implement explicit online identification baseline
Technical / research work: Estimate actuator scale or dynamics parameters from transitions and condition a controller/policy on that estimate.
Exit criterion: Estimator error and convergence time are logged alongside task performance.
Relationship / public action: Ask a controls mentor to critique identifiability and estimator assumptions.

Title: Week 11: Compare temporal fault profiles
Technical / research work: Run matched-budget comparisons under fixed, sudden, and gradual faults; inspect whether memory helps or lags.
Exit criterion: Preliminary plots for H1, H2, and H4 with documented failures.
Relationship / public action: Mentor review #2; shortlist realistic workshop/student/reproducibility venues.

Title: Week 12: Midpoint replication and scope cut
Technical / research work: Reproduce one result cleanly; remove weak fault families, methods, or environments.
Exit criterion: v0.2 release and three-page midpoint report with limitations and revised compute forecast.
Relationship / public action: Share one useful result with a PhD student or engineer working on adaptive control.

Title: Week 13: Freeze the final evaluation protocol
Technical / research work: Commit hypotheses, metrics, held-out severities, abrupt onset distributions, seed count, and exclusion rules.
Exit criterion: Versioned protocol exists before final experiments begin.
Relationship / public action: Publish the protocol and invite methodological criticism.

Title: Week 14: Run final comparison batch A
Technical / research work: Compare classical, feed-forward PPO, recurrent PPO, and explicit identification with automatic provenance.
Exit criterion: Complete raw nominal and in-distribution results for all final seeds.
Relationship / public action: Offer a small, relevant control/embedded contribution to a local project.

Title: Week 15: Run held-out fault generalization
Technical / research work: Evaluate unseen fault severity, onset timing, payload/friction, bias, and latency within frozen scope.
Exit criterion: Held-out results with confidence intervals and no selective seed reporting.
Relationship / public action: Discuss one reproduced paper result with its first author or maintainer.

Title: Week 16: Analyze adaptation and memory failure modes
Technical / research work: Measure recovery/adaptation time and identify cases where stale memory harms behavior.
Exit criterion: Quantified failure taxonomy with at least three recurring modes and representative rollouts.
Relationship / public action: Share an honest negative or mixed result publicly.

Title: Week 17: Add at most one justified extension
Technical / research work: Choose Reacher-to-second-environment transfer, compact transformer if GPU exists, or safe HIL if hardware exists; otherwise improve analysis.
Exit criterion: Extension is completed or explicitly rejected by week end without delaying the core study.
Relationship / public action: Mentor review #3 on whether evidence is submission-worthy.

Title: Week 18: Perform independent clean reproduction
Technical / research work: Install from scratch and reproduce one headline result using committed config and data pipeline.
Exit criterion: Independent/clean rerun matches expected tolerance; documentation and tests are complete.
Relationship / public action: Follow up with prior reviewers using the improved artifact.

Title: Week 19: Write paper structure and methods
Technical / research work: Draft abstract, introduction, related work, benchmark, methods, and protocol; place all planned figures/tables.
Exit criterion: Complete paper skeleton with every claim mapped to evidence.
Relationship / public action: Recruit one controls reviewer and one ML reviewer.

Title: Week 20: Write results and limitations
Technical / research work: Complete results, discussion, safety, limitations, compute statement, and reproducibility checklist.
Exit criterion: Draft v1 contains no placeholder results or unsupported claims.
Relationship / public action: Publish a progress note focused on one defensible finding.

Title: Week 21: Address reviews and necessary reruns
Technical / research work: Resolve methodological concerns; rerun only experiments needed for a documented question.
Exit criterion: Draft v2 and response-to-feedback log are complete.
Relationship / public action: If directly relevant, send one artifact-based note to an appropriate senior target.

Title: Week 22: Release FaultAdapt-Gym v1.0
Technical / research work: Publish code, configs, allowed data, report, demo, citation, and archival release if possible.
Exit criterion: v1.0 release, 3–5 minute demo, project page, and 6–8 page report.
Relationship / public action: Submit only to a mentor-approved credible venue if evidence and timing fit.

Title: Week 23: Prepare targeted outreach and applications
Technical / research work: Create academic CV, industry résumé, project one-pager, research statement paragraph, and contact tracker.
Exit criterion: Complete application packet grounded in the released artifact.
Relationship / public action: Contact 2–3 relevant people with distinct evidence-based reasons.

Title: Week 24: Integrate portfolio and choose next experiment
Technical / research work: Give a mock talk, conduct retrospective, and decide whether GPU/VLA or hardware validation is the next controlled extension.
Exit criterion: Final dashboard, mock talk, lessons learned, and next six-month milestone.
Relationship / public action: Thank contributors and update people whose earlier feedback changed the work.
